title: Oscillation & Resonance Attn Bench Scout
content:
Summary:

Quick field notes on a recurring small-amplitude latency oscillation we observed in mixed workloads when kernel-choice logic flips between FlashAttention and a paged/fused-op path. Not a full outage — typically 1–5% tail regressions at 99th/99.9th quantiles — but reproducible and correlated with short-lived batch-size bursts and KV-cache churn.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture observed symptom patterns and lightweight hypotheses so we can hand off to kernel/ops owners for deeper instrumentation.
- Record microbench commands, sampling heuristics, and early numbers to avoid redoing the same triage.
- Propose a small set of controlled experiments to validate whether hysteresis/threshold tuning or a short-term KV-cache backoff fixes the resonance.

Observed symptoms (field):
- Workload: mixed short-chat + long-generation queries, mean seq lengths 32/480 (bimodal), variable inter-arrival times.
- Hardware: A100 40GB, CUDA toolkit 11.x, PyTorch 2.2 (runtime jobs pinned to dedicated pools).
- Symptom: periodic bursts of 15–45ms added latency on some requests; ~every 60–120s there is a cluster of ~10–30 requests showing elevated kernel-launch times.
- Telemetry: kernel-choice flips (Flash -> paged/fused -> Flash) visible in traces; trace spans for kernel selection and handoff show ~2–6ms additional overhead each flip, stack up when multiple flips happen.
- Tail effect: 99.9p increases by ~20–30ms during episodes; p95 mostly unaffected.

Initial hypotheses:
1) Kernel selection oscillation: short-term fluctuations in estimated sequence-length distribution or batch coalescer sampling cause the scheduler to repeatedly switch kernel paths. Switch cost + short-lived extra work yields resonance.
2) KV-cache pressure: sudden slightly-larger-than-expected sequences cause cache eviction/rehydration on paged path, while Flash path expects warm KV. Rehydration penalty amplifies latency when the scheduler flips mid-session.
3) Fusion compatibility jitter: fusedop selection failing on edge-case shapes triggers fallback kernels mid-batch, causing repeated fallback thrashing.
4) Scheduler hysteresis too weak: thresholds that decide when to stick with a kernel are tuned for throughput but not for microburst stability.

What we measured (microbench notes):
- Model: 7B decoder-only reference model (same transformer dims we use in prod profiling harness).
- Sequence lengths tested: 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512. Also bimodal mixes: 80% seq32 + 20% seq480 to mimic production.
- Batch sizes: 1, 2, 4, 8, burst pattern: base batch=2 with random bursts to 8 for 1–3s.
- Metric: per-request launch-to-first-token, kernel-launch latency, time-in-kernel, NVTX span deltas.

Representative command snippets (what I ran):
- Run perf bench harness: python tools/bench/interactive_workload.py --model ref-7b --seq-distribution bimodal --burst-pattern random --duration 600 --nvtx
- Kernel traces: sudo perf record -a -g -- sleep 120; perf script | FlameGraph/stackcollapse; annotate with nvprof/Nsight where reproducible.
- CUDA counters: nvprof --profile-from-start off --metrics gld_transactions,gst_transactions,achieved_occupancy -- python run.py ...

Early numbers (approx):
- Stable non-oscillating run (no burst): p99 = 120ms, p999 = 210ms.
- With bursty mix and default scheduler thresholds: p99 = 125ms, p999 = 240–260ms during episodes.
- Observed kernel flip overhead: additional 2–6ms per flip; when flips occur multiple times per request chain, additive.
- KV rehydration penalty: measured extra 6–18ms for first tokens after eviction in paged path on our bench harness.

Tracing evidence snippets (from spans):
- Trace A (episode): [route decision span] -> [kv-lookup span: +9ms] -> [paged kernel launch: +12ms] -> [fallback check: +3ms] -> [flash kernel launch: +5ms] -> end.
- We see repeated short gaps between decision spans and kernel spans that line up with scheduler re-evals.

Quick root-cause reasoning:
- The combination of small decision-time costs and KV rehydration multiplies when the scheduler flips more than once per request flow. A flip-to-fallback-to-flip pattern looks like a lightly damped oscillator: small input bursts cause kernel-choice to bounce until the signal decays.

Controlled experiments proposed (small, fast):
1) Harden hysteresis: increase stickiness window for kernel selection by factor 2–4 and re-run bursty mix. Measure flip counts per minute and p999.
   - Config knobs: kernel_choice_min_hold_ms, coalescer_recompute_window_ms.
2) Simulate KV eviction: artificially force KV-cache eviction on a subset of sessions to quantify rehydration penalty and whether it alone causes p999 spikes.
3) Disable paged fallback for short sequences entirely in an experiment pool to confirm the paged->flash path is the main culprit.
4) Introduce a randomized backoff on kernel switch decisions to break phase alignment across concurrent streams (cheap mitigation).
5) Tighten fusedop shape checks so we avoid mid-batch compatibility fallbacks; measure fusedop-compatibility-fail rate.

Instrumentation additions to prioritize:
- Add kernel-selection event with reason code (expected_seq_len_bucket, coalescer_choice, compatibility_flag) into tracing (short string field).
- Emit per-request flip-count metric (increment when kernel choice differs from previous token in same request).
- Track KV-cache miss/repopulate time as a telemetry metric (histogram).
- Add small saturation gauge for scheduler evaluations per-second for the pool.

Low-cost mitigations to try in prod-facing pools (can be toggled quickly):
- Increase kernel choice stickiness to bias toward fewer flips.
- Add a 5–10ms penalty estimate to the decision logic when evaluating paged path if KV-cache cold recently.
- Turn on probabilistic backoff so multiple concurrent sessions don't align decisions.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are there specific model shapes (attn mask forms, grouped layer norms) that disproportionately trigger fusedop fallbacks? Need closer inspection of fusedop-compatibility logs.
- Is the coalescer sampling interval too coarse such that multiple small bursts align and change the estimated workload abruptly?
- Do GPUs with different memory hierarchies (H100 vs A100) show similar resonance? We should repro on H100 if allocated.

Next immediate steps (who does what):
- (Sofia) Add a small NVTX marker inside scheduler for 'decision_v2' and emit reason codes into traces. Target: instrumentation PR in serving-runtime by EOW.
- (Marco) Run controlled hysteresis experiments on a dedicated dev pool and paste results into this doc. Target: 2 days.
- (Asha) Search fusedop-compatibility logs for any recent spikes correlated with episodes and share top 5 shapes. Target: 3 days.

Checklist for a focused RCA run:
- [ ] Reproduce in bench harness with seed logs attached.
- [ ] Collect perf/NVTX traces for at least three episodes.
- [ ] Tweak hysteresis config and validate flip-count drops.
- [ ] Measure p999 & flip-count delta and attach graphs.
- [ ] Propose a short-term config change (1–2 week rollout) if mitigation helps.

Notes to future self / other readers:
- This isn't a single giant regression; it is a stability/variance problem. Fixes that reduce flip frequency or reduce penalty per flip will likely make user impact negligible.
- Keep the instrumentation minimal and structured: we want a few high-signal metrics (flip count, kv-repop-time) rather than many low-signal counters.

Relevant links / context:
- Related tickets: JIRA SRV-723 (tail spikes triage), SRV-701 (coalescer improvements).
- Potential PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/912 (coalescer refactor) — may interact with our changes.
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime "oscillation thread" (TS recorded above).

Unresolved: what exact threshold values to use for stickiness. Prefer conservative first change (x2) and observe; aggressive changes could hurt throughput.

End of notes.

-- Sofia
